## Why this needs its own mechanism

[rhino](https://appsilon.github.io/rhino/) apps (and any app using [`{box}`](https://klmr.me/box/) modules directly) load their code through `box::use()`, not `base::source()`. `shiny.cov`'s `source()` override never sees that code at all, so it needs a second, separate hook.

There's also a real, existing tool for *part* of this problem: `covr::package_coverage()` (or rhino's own `rhino::covr_r()` wrapper around `covr::file_coverage()`) already gives genuinely exact, real branch-level R coverage for a rhino app's server-side logic -- when tests are written with `shiny::testServer()`, which runs the server function directly in-process with no browser and no separate R process involved. If that's all you need, use `rhino::covr_r()` directly; `shiny.cov` isn't necessary for it and doesn't try to replace it.

Where `rhino::covr_r()` can't help at all is real UI-driven testing -- `shinytest2::AppDriver`, Cypress, or Playwright, which all spawn the Shiny process in a genuinely separate process to serve a real browser. That's exactly the case `shiny.cov` exists for, and it works for `{box}`/rhino apps too, not just plain `app.R` apps.

## Setup

No different from a plain app -- `shiny.cov::setup()` detects rhino's `app.R` (which is just `rhino::app()`) the same way it detects any other `app.R`:

```r
shiny.cov::setup("my-rhino-app")

app <- shiny.cov::AppDriver$new("my-rhino-app")
app$set_inputs("app-name" = "Alice")
app$click(selector = "#app-greet")
app$stop()

cov <- shiny.cov::collect("my-rhino-app")
covr::report(cov)
```

## How it works

The bootstrap patches `box:::load_from_source()` -- the function `{box}` itself uses to parse and evaluate every module file -- so each module gets the same branch-level instrumentation (shiny.cov's own AST tracer, ported in-tree from `{covr}` -- see `R/trace.R`) as a `source()`d file, surgically (only the parse-and-eval step is replaced; `{box}`'s own export scanning and S3 method registration are left alone).

For the UI manifest: a rhino app's `ui` is a `function(id)`, not a static tag object, and it's never a top-level variable anywhere reachable from the app's entry point -- it lives inside `app/main.R`'s own module namespace, which would make it awkward to find by inspecting R-side code at all. `shiny.cov` doesn't try to -- the manifest is discovered from the *live browser* instead, by asking Shiny's own `Shiny.inputBindings`/`Shiny.outputBindings` registry what's actually rendered on the page (see `vignette("shinytest2")`/`vignette("cypress")`). This works identically for a rhino app's namespaced ids (`"app-name"`, `"app-greet"`, ...) as for any other app -- the discovery script doesn't know or care that `ui` was a function living inside a module namespace, only what actually ended up in the DOM.

Module boundaries (`manifest$modules`, and each element's `module` field) come from a `shiny::moduleServer()` hook instead, recording the real namespace prefix (e.g. `"app"`) at the point `logic$welcome_server(id)` calls it -- ground truth, not inferred from splitting an id on `-`.

## Action buttons and other widgets are fully discovered

A manifest built by matching Shiny's `shiny-input-container` CSS class in the server-side R tag tree would miss `shiny::actionButton()`, which doesn't carry that class -- so a rhino module's `greet`/`reset` buttons would never show up in a manifest built that way.

The browser-registry discovery described above doesn't have this gap: every real Shiny input, including action buttons, must register with `Shiny.inputBindings` for Shiny's client-server protocol to work at all, so it's found the same way any other input is, with zero special-casing. This also means it isn't limited to base Shiny widgets -- a rhino app using a third-party widget library (`shinyWidgets`, `shiny.fluent`, or any custom `Shiny.inputBindings.register()` call) is discovered the exact same way.

## Example: box module structure

```
my-rhino-app/
├── app.R              # rhino::app()
├── rhino.yml
├── config.yml
├── app/
│   ├── main.R          # ui <- function(id) {...}; server <- function(id) {...}
│   ├── static/
│   ├── logic/
│   │   └── welcome.R    # #' @export
│   │                      welcome_server <- function(id) {...}
│   └── view/
│       └── welcome.R    # #' @export
│                          welcome_ui <- function(id) {...}
└── tests/
    └── testthat/
        ├── setup-shinytest2.R
        └── test-app.R
```

## Troubleshooting

### Coverage is empty or only covers definitions, never reactive code

Confirm `shiny.cov` is actually **installed**, not just loaded via `pkgload::load_all()` -- the box hook runs inside the child process, which needs `requireNamespace("shiny.cov")` to succeed there independently of the parent session. `shiny.cov::setup()` warns about this at setup time.

### `box::use()` fails with "unable to load module"

This is a `{box}`/rhino configuration issue, not a `shiny.cov` one -- `box.path` needs to be set to the project root (rhino apps normally do this via `.Rprofile`: `options(box.path = getwd())`). Confirm `box::use()` works for your app *without* `shiny.cov::setup()` involved before reporting a coverage issue.
